\"מלאכי שביל\" הם תושבים ביישובים לאורך: "Trail angels" are residents of communities along the Israel National Trail route who have chosen to host hikers, usually for free or for a token payment. The phenomenon grew with the trail's rising popularity, and SPNI (the Israel Trails Committee) maintains an official list divided by region, from Dan to Eilat. According to ISRAEL21c the network currently numbers about 450–500 hosts (in 2012 there were about 100 registered). What they offer: in most cases a shower, a spot for a tent in the yard or a mattress/bed in a room, water, phone charging; some offer laundry, a hot meal, coffee, and sometimes a yurt/cabin dedicated to hikers (for example the 'Angels' Cabin' in Sansana, the hikers' cabin in Tzukim). Some hosts offer only a shower/water without lodging (according to SPNI guidelines, hosting without lodging or a shower is not included in the official list). Cost: most angels ask for nothing; some ask for a token donation (according to Bex Band: 20–80 ILS per person when they ask); according to shvil.fandom, places charging up to ~15 ILS are still listed in the angels list, and above that they are considered 'cheap paid lodging'. In the Negev some of the 'services' (meals in Shaharut, shuttles, water caching) are paid. Making contact: phone/WhatsApp in advance (preferably by message, 24–48 hours ahead, not late at night); in some communities (for example Kibbutz Dan) you temporarily join the community's WhatsApp group and write your arrival date, number of people and what you need. The lists change frequently — hosts stop hosting, so always verify. The SPNI list is updated by the hosts themselves by email at shvil@spni.org.il or via WhatsApp. For English-speaking hikers: israeltrail.net maintains a list in English (it claims to be the only up-to-date one), and shvil.fandom.com (INT Trail Angels) and israelbylocals.com also present lists — but they themselves note that they are not managed by the angels and are not necessarily up to date.

המדריך הרשמי של החברה להגנת הטבע מחלק את: The official SPNI guide divides the trail into 56 segments from north to south (typical hiking days); the 'Red Book' and other maps use a different numbering (60+ days).

מקטעים רבים של השביל בנגב ובכרמל עוברים: Many segments of the trail in the Negev and the Carmel pass through reserves – a full thru-hike with a dog requires detours/coordination; in summer and late spring the dog suffers from heat and thorns; water for the dog doubles the water weight.

הצפון באוקטובר עדיין יבש וחם-נעים, ומגיע: The north in October is still dry and pleasantly warm, and you reach the Negev in November–December when the heat breaks. The downside: short days (10 hours of daylight in December), rain and storms in the north from November, and desert flash floods right in the transition season.
מתכננים יום מנוחה: אצל מלאך שביל, בחניון: Plan a rest day: at a trail angel's, at an overnight campsite or in a community, with food bought in advance. No buses from Friday afternoon until Saturday night; on Yom Kippur everything is closed; on Passover and Sukkot the outdoors are crowded and opening hours are irregular.

הסימון לבן-כחול-כתום. המוסכמה: כשהפס הלב: The marking is white-blue-orange. The convention: when the white stripe 'leads'/is on top – you are heading north (toward the snowy Hermon); when the orange leads – south (toward the Negev). This is an unofficial convention – the Trails Committee stresses that the colors only identify the trail; navigate by map/GPS.
בצפון ובמרכז כמעט כל יום יש יישוב עם מכו: In the north and center almost every day there is a community with a grocery store (limited hours in kibbutzim, closed on Shabbat). South of Arad only: Sde Boker, Mitzpe Ramon, Sapir/Ein Yahav (detour), Neot Smadar/Shaharut, Be'er Ora. Arad is the last major resupply point.
מתחילים במדבר כשהוא קריר ופורח, ומגיעים: You start in the desert while it is cool and in bloom, and reach the north when the Galilee is green and relatively dry. The later you leave (after mid-March), the more you risk sharav and heat of 35°C+ in the Arava and the makhteshim even before reaching Arad. Another advantage: the days get longer over the course of the trek.
הטמנה עצמית: קוברים בקבוקי 1.5 ל' / ג'רי: Self-caching: bury 1.5 L bottles / a 5–6 L jerrycan about 30–40 cm deep in the ground, under a shrub or at the base of a rock, marked with your name and date, and record the GPS coordinates + a photo. Do not cache in a streambed (flash floods), and do not mark too conspicuously (theft/animals).
תחזית השירות המטאורולוגי (ims.gov.il) וא: Israel Meteorological Service forecast (ims.gov.il) and INPA warnings (*3639, parks.org.il) a day or two before; in the rainy season (November–March, and sometimes April) do not sleep in a streambed and do not cross a flowing wadi. The flood arrives from distant rain – even under clear skies.
חלקית בלבד: ברוב שמורות הטבע בתשלום ובחנ: Only partially: in most paid nature reserves and at paid overnight campsites dogs are not allowed; in national parks they are allowed on a leash and muzzled. In the Negev and the Carmel the trail passes through many reserves – detours are required; heat and thorns make it hard. On the north/coast stretches – easier.
